newsitem.title: TURKEY: Istanbul shares gain 1.95 pct to new record.
newsitem.headline: Istanbul shares gain 1.95 pct to new record.

text.p: Turkish shares posted gains in selective and quiet trade on Thursday, following a five-day new year holiday, but volume was weak, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 closed at a new all-time high of 995, up 19 points, or 1.95 percent from the December 27 closing of 976 which was the previous record.

The old composite index (IMKB-100) which hit a record high 97,588.80 on December 27, was divided by 100, resulting in a 1986 base value of one instead of 100 as part of the Exchange's move to simplify existing indices and introduce new ones.
Trade volume shrank to 8.55 trillion lira from 11.40 on December 27 when the market closed for the new year holiday.
Of the 231 shares traded, gainers outdid losers by 144 to 39 and 48 closed steady.

"The rise was based on activity in the shares of largely state-owned firms and a few others, although overall volume was thin. The market tried to adapt to changes in index values," said Nermin Samiloglu from Tacirler securities.

The December 27 closing values of the industrial and financial indices were also divided by 100 and several new indices were created to represent a services sector. There are also sub-sectors classified under industrial, financial and services, investment trusts and regional and new company markets.

The industrial index ended at 1,071, up 2.39 percent from the modified December 27 close of 1,046. The financial index gained 2.19 percent from last Friday's modified close of 914 to end at 934. The services index finished at 1,039, compared to an opening of 1,046.
